hints.content:
###The strategy

$\text{Area of a triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot \text{base} \cdot \text{height}$

Before we can apply the formula to find the area of $\triangle ABC$, we must find the base and height of the triangle using the Pythagorean theorem (or the distance formula).

* The base is the length $AC$.
* The height is the length $AB$.

###Step 1: Find the length $AC$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} 
AC^2&= {\redE{6}^2 +\redE{15}^2 }  &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
AC&= \sqrt{\redE{6}^2 +\redE{15}^2 }  &&\text{Square root both sides}\\\\
&=\sqrt{261} \\\\
&=\sqrt{9\cdot29} \\\\
&=\tealE{3\sqrt{29}}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Right Triangle A B C has point A at one, eight, point B at six, six, and point C at negative five, negative seven. A horizontal line of six units connects from point A to a vertical line of fifteen units connecting to point C.

hints.content:
###Step 2: Find the length $AB$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} 
AB^2&= \redE{5}^2 +\redE{2}^2  &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
AB&= \sqrt{\redE{5}^2 +\redE{2}^2 } &&\text{Square root both sides} \\\\
&=\goldE{\sqrt{29}}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Right Triangle A B C has point A at one, eight, point B at six, six, and point C at negative five, negative seven. A horizontal line of five units connects from point A to a vertical line of two units connecting to point B.

hints.content:
###Step 3: Find the area of the triangle

Using the base and height of $\triangle ABC$, we can find the area:

$\begin{align} \text{Area of a triangle} &= \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot \text{base} \cdot \text{height}\\\\
&= \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot AC\cdot AB \\\\
&= \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot(\tealE{3\sqrt{29}})\cdot(\goldE{\sqrt{29}}) \\\\
&= \dfrac{3}{2}\cdot\sqrt{29}\cdot\sqrt{29} \\\\
&= \dfrac{3}{2}\cdot29 \\\\
&= \dfrac{87}{2}
\end{align}$

###The answer:

The area of $\triangle ABC$ is $43.5$ units$^2$.

[[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
Yes, we can find the area of the outer rectangle, then subtract the areas of the triangular regions outside of $\triangle ABC$.



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}_{\triangle ABC} &= 11(15) - \text{Area}_{\triangle1} - \text{Area}_{\triangle2} - \text{Area}_{\triangle3} \\\\
&=165 - \dfrac{1}{2}(5)(2)-\dfrac{1}{2}(11)(13)-\dfrac{1}{2}(6)(15)\\\\
&=165 - 5-71.5-45\\\\
&=43.5
\end{align}$

The area of $\triangle ABC$ is $43.5$ units$^2$.
